verdict.root_cause: An automated environment change set cartservice's REDIS_ADDR to redis-cart:6380 at 18:37:55, about two minutes before onset [tr_357d9c0d9bd1]. cartservice cannot connect to that endpoint, and since the connection is made during process initialization (Main -> InitializeAsync -> EnsureRedisConnected), the failure throws an unhandled exception and kills the process, leaving a crash loop still active at window end [tr_8cc792d6a61f]. With cartservice unable to serve gRPC calls, checkoutservice's CartService/GetCart call is the error-bearing leaf span in all 10 sampled traces, propagating up through PlaceOrder to the frontend [tr_38fa477ad955], and checkoutservice's error ratio steps off a flat-zero baseline at 18:38:45 [tr_b3910e6d922e]. The wrong address value is itself the mechanism.
verdict.reasoning: Direction: the error originates at the deepest span, checkoutservice's GetCart into cartservice, and propagates upward to frontend, which holds negligible self time [tr_38fa477ad955]; checkoutservice logs show no errors and no restarts, only missing downstream completion lines after 18:39:40 [tr_a3115dfb62d3], and it has no change of its own [tr_fdfef69d1dae]. So the alerting services are noticers. Mechanism: cartservice logs name a failed connection to redis-cart on port 6380 throwing from initialization, repeatedly [tr_8cc792d6a61f], which explains why GetCart fails in 1.4-3.6ms rather than timing out [tr_38fa477ad955]. Trigger and timing: the change installed that exact endpoint at 18:37:55 and the checkoutservice change point is 18:38:45 [tr_357d9c0d9bd1, tr_b3910e6d922e]. Rival cartservice triggers are excluded by the same record: last image change was a revert 5.1 hours earlier, and the delay-injecting sidecar was removed nine minutes before onset [tr_357d9c0d9bd1]. bad_config rather than dependency_latency or resource_exhaustion because no waiting and no resource ceiling is involved - the value names an endpoint that does not accept the connection, and restoring the prior REDIS_ADDR ends the crash loop.
open_questions: Nobody probed redis-cart itself. If the cache legitimately moved to 6380 and the instance is down or not listening, the fault is the store's availability rather than the address value.
cartservice call metrics returned no samples in either window [tr_584aeb4b9afb], so onset timing and the crash loop have no independent metric corroboration.

checkoutservice's error ratio peaks near 0.67 rather than 1.0 [tr_b3910e6d922e] while cartservice appears fully down; what carried the successful checkouts is unexplained, and both log results were truncated across roughly 18:10-18:39 [tr_a3115dfb62d3, tr_8cc792d6a61f].

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart is correctly addressed at 6380 but the Redis instance is unreachable or not running, so cartservice's startup connection fails for reasons outside its config.
alternatives.why_not: Not excluded, since no dispatch touched redis-cart - but the address value changed 50 seconds before onset and the failing target is exactly the value that change installed, which makes the edit the more economical explanation.

alternatives.root_cause: Residual network state from the traffic-shaping sidecar removed nine minutes before onset is blocking or delaying cartservice's egress to Redis.
alternatives.why_not: The sidecar was withdrawn before onset [tr_357d9c0d9bd1], and the checkout failures are fast errors rather than timeouts [tr_38fa477ad955]; the failure is a process crash on connect, not a wait.

proposal.expected_effect: Reverting cartservice's environment to its pre-18:37:55 state removes the REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6380 override and recreates the container against the previously-working default Redis endpoint. Observable: (1) in cart-service logs, the repeating cycle of 'connection attempt -> failure to connect -> unhandled ApplicationException -> restart' seen from 18:40:06 to 18:42:14 stops, replaced by a single successful startup followed by ordinary AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync lines with no error severity [tr_8cc792d6a61f]; (2) checkoutservice's error ratio returns from its 0.067 mean / 0.67 peak to the flat zero of its pre-18:38:45 baseline [tr_b3910e6d922e]; (3) newly sampled checkout traces no longer carry ERROR on the checkoutservice CartService/GetCart leaf span, and PlaceOrder traces extend past prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart into payment/currency spans that are currently absent [tr_38fa477ad955]. Note cartservice's own call metrics returned no samples in either window [tr_584aeb4b9afb], so cartservice-side confirmation must come from logs, not metrics.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, within ~2 minutes of the recreate, cart-service logs show the same EnsureRedisConnected/InitializeAsync ApplicationException cycle continuing against the reverted address — that would mean the redis-cart instance itself is unavailable and the port value was not the fault (the open question: nobody probed redis-cart). Also falsified if the crash loop stops but checkoutservice's error ratio stays elevated, which would mean GetCart was only one of several failure paths and something else carried the ~33% of checkouts that kept succeeding — an unexplained gap in the current diagnosis. A third falsifier: the REDIS_ADDR=6380 value reappears shortly after revert, since all 13 recorded changes come from platform-automation on a recurring set/revert cycle [tr_357d9c0d9bd1]; then the fix is to stop the pipeline, which is outside this system's actions.
proposal.risk: If the cache legitimately moved to port 6380 and the 6380 listener is simply down, this revert points cartservice at an endpoint that is also not listening and the crash loop continues — no recovery, and roughly one extra restart cycle of downtime. The recreate itself terminates the current process mid-flight, discarding any in-process cart state (cache only for this service). If the automated pipeline re-applies the 6380 value, the config will flap between two states and cartservice may crash-loop through several more cycles rather than settling. Reverting also silently undoes whatever the pipeline intended, so if 6380 was a deliberate migration step this hides the real problem instead of fixing it.
proposal.blast_radius: One service, cartservice. Its inbound caller checkoutservice, and frontend above it, see connection resets on CartService/GetCart for the duration of the container recreate — the same call that is already failing in all 10 sampled traces [tr_38fa477ad955], so the marginal harm to callers is small but not zero. loadgenerator's checkout path sees the same brief reset. Because the reverted value is a dependency address, the Redis instance at the previous endpoint sees cart traffic return, and redis-cart:6380 stops receiving connection attempts.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity with simultaneous checkout and frontend alerts plus loadgenerator impact indicates a real user-facing failure, not a lone latency warning. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the shared downstream set gives no single fault signature yet.
